qs.q: U3 Part1 (1). ( ) is used to produce a wearable layer of protection from harmful chemicals.
qs.note: 本文：coating is made from a metal-organic framework that snags and breaks down harmful compounds。bは効果の言い換え、cは無関係の例。

qs.q: U3 Part1 (2). Nanowires in the new fabric are expected to ( ).
opts: block the visible light by generating electricity
keep the wearers warm by using their body heat
reflect infrared waves by embedding them in the material
qs.ans: keep the wearers warm by using their body heat
qs.note: 本文：Fabric embedded with nanowires could reflect your body heat back onto your skin／electric current could provide warmth。他は別パラグラフ（光を通す布）の内容との混同。

qs.q: U3 Part2 (1). Triboelectric materials and piezoelectric materials help the researchers ( ).
opts: create a new type of solar panel
qs.note: 摩擦電気・圧電性の素材は「身につけるだけで発電する」服＝self-powered outfitsの開発につながる。aはソーラーパネルの話と混同。

qs.q: U3 Part2 (2). It is expected that ( ) in future.
opts: conductive thread stitched into a t-shirt will soak up the sun
data-packed fabric could be replaced by a hands-free key
the newly developed fabrics with various functions will go on the market
qs.ans: the newly developed fabrics with various functions will go on the market
qs.note: 最終段落：still pretty far from hitting retail racks／inventors hope... could someday let you get more from your wardrobe＝将来的に市販化される見込み。

qs.q: U4 Part1 (1). Groundwater ( ).
opts: is not found in desert areas
qs.note: 本文：groundwater lurks（隠れている）under mountains, plains and even deserts。aは真逆、cは「砂漠にもある」に反する。

qs.q: U4 Part1 (2). People can use groundwater to ( ).
qs.note: 本文：people extract groundwater through wells for drinking, sanitation, watering crops（作物＝食料生産）など。wellsは地下水を汲み上げる手段であり用途ではない。

qs.q: U4 Part2 (1). Data from satellites reveal that ( ).
opts: the number of aquifers is decreasing
more than half of the aquifers in the U.S. are in danger
qs.note: 本文：Twenty-one of Earth’s 37 biggest aquifers are shrinking, satellite data show。「数が減っている」のではなく「縮小している」が正しい。

qs.q: U4 Part2 (2). The decrease in the amount of groundwater ( ).
opts: triggers big earthquakes around the world
qs.note: 本文：they hold less water to refill rivers and streams, threatening freshwater ecosystems。地震はCaliforniaでの"small earthquakes"のみで「世界的な大地震」ではない。

qs.q: Our clothes keep us warm in the winter or cool while we're working out.
Clothes let each of us express our unique sense of style.
Some researchers think our clothes could be doing even more.
Doctors and lawyers are dreaming up new ways to make clothes safer.
qs.note: 本文は Those scientists and engineers。doctors/lawyers は登場しない。

qs.q: The passage says clothes could be made safer, comfier, or more expensive.
qs.note: 本文は safer, comfier, or just more convenient。expensive ではない。

qs.q: The passage states that clothes cannot express our personal style.
qs.note: 本文は真逆：They let each of us express our unique sense of style。

qs.q: One new shoe design features pop-out spikes on the sole that grip the ground.
A new fabric coating could absorb and neutralize some chemical weapons.
The fabric coating is made from a metal-organic framework.
The pop-out spikes are located on the toe of the shoe, not the sole.
qs.note: 本文は on the sole（靴底）。toe（つま先）ではない。

qs.q: The coating could offer a heavyweight shield to people in war-torn countries.
qs.note: 本文は a lightweight shield（軽量の盾）。heavyweight ではない。

qs.q: The metal-organic framework creates harmful compounds instead of breaking them down.
qs.note: 本文は真逆：snags and breaks down harmful compounds（有害な化合物を分解する）。

qs.q: Not all advanced attire is designed to save lives.
Fabric embedded with nanowires could reflect your body heat back onto your skin.
This heat-generating fabric may be especially useful for people working in hot deserts.
qs.note: 本文は super cold conditions（極寒の環境）。hot deserts ではない。

qs.q: Electric current humming through the metal threads could cool the wearer down.
qs.note: 本文は真逆：could provide warmth（暖かさを与える）。

qs.q: Only hikers, and no one else, could benefit from this fabric.
qs.note: 本文は hikers, soldiers, or others working in super cold conditions と複数の対象を挙げている。

qs.q: Another new fabric traps very little body heat.
Tiny pores in this material let infrared waves pass through it.
The waves that pass through the material carry heat away from the body to keep you cool.
This material is see-through because it does not block visible light.
qs.note: 本文は逆：pores block visible light waves — so the material isn’t see-through。

qs.q: This fabric is designed to keep the wearer as warm as possible.
qs.note: この段落の布は熱を逃がして涼しく保つためのもの（前段落と対照的）。

qs.q: The tiny pores block infrared waves and let visible light pass through.
qs.note: 本文は逆：visible light を block し、infrared waves を通す。

qs.q: Some researchers have dreamt up wholly new uses for clothing, like turning wearers into walking power outlets.
Triboelectric materials can generate electricity when bent or flexed.
Piezoelectric materials produce a charge when squeezed or twisted.
The future of fashion is only about improving garments' existing functions.
qs.note: 本文は not just about improving garments’ existing functions。

qs.q: Flexible solar panels sewn into fabric could soak up moonlight to recharge phones.
qs.note: 本文は soak up the sun（太陽光）。moonlight ではない。

qs.q: Friction between different parts of a material reduces triboelectric charge.
qs.note: 本文は真逆：friction builds up charge（摩擦が電荷を生む）。

qs.q: In one experiment, researchers stitched conductive thread into a t-shirt.
This turned the shirt into an antenna that could send signals to a smartphone.
Data-packed fabric could be used as a hands-free key or form of ID.
Another team threaded fabric with magnetized gold and platinum to write data into fabrics.
qs.note: 本文は magnetized copper and silver（銅と銀）。gold/platinum ではない。

qs.q: While some fabrics help charge devices, no fabric could ever serve as a device itself.
qs.note: 本文は真逆：others could serve as devices themselves。

qs.q: The conductive thread experiment turned the shirt into a solar panel.
qs.note: 本文は antenna（アンテナ）。solar panel ではない。

qs.q: Many of these ideas have not yet left the lab.
They're still pretty far from hitting retail racks.
Inventors hope these innovations could someday let you get more from your wardrobe.
These smart-clothing innovations are already sold widely in stores.
qs.note: 本文は逆：still pretty far from hitting retail racks（まだ店頭には程遠い）。

qs.q: The passage says none of these ideas will ever leave the laboratory.
qs.note: 本文は not yet left the lab（まだ）であり、将来市場に出ることを inventors hope している。

qs.q: Almost all of the world's liquid freshwater lies underground.
This stash beneath our feet is called groundwater.
Walking over water is truly a miracle with no scientific explanation.
qs.note: 本文は「奇跡のようだが実は地下水の上を歩いているだけ」と科学的に説明している。

qs.q: Groundwater is a stash of freshwater found floating in the sky.
qs.note: 本文は beneath our feet（足元の地下）。空ではない。

qs.q: Only a small fraction of the world's liquid freshwater lies underground.
qs.note: 本文は almost all（ほとんど全て）。

qs.q: Most of Earth's H2O is in the oceans.
Only about 2.5 percent of the planet's water is freshwater.
About 30 percent of Earth's freshwater is groundwater.
Nearly 69 percent of Earth's freshwater flows through rivers and fills lakes.
qs.note: 69%は氷河・氷冠に凍っている割合。川と湖はmeagerな1.2%。

qs.q: Rivers and lakes hold much more freshwater than groundwater does.
qs.note: 本文は逆：groundwater(約30%) は rivers and lakes(1.2%) よりずっと多い。

qs.q: Groundwater is found almost everywhere on Earth, including under deserts.
Together, aquifers hold about 60 times as much water as the world's lakes and rivers combined.
Groundwater is never found under deserts.
qs.note: 本文は逆：lurks under mountains, plains and even deserts。

qs.q: Tiny gaps between rocks and soil grains repel water like a raincoat.
qs.note: 本文は逆：soak up and hold this water like a sponge（スポンジのように吸い込んで保持する）。

qs.q: Aquifers hold about 60 times as much water as the world's oceans.
qs.note: 本文は lakes and rivers combined（湖と川の合計）。oceans ではない。

qs.q: Rain and melted snow seep down into the ground.
Groundwater can stay underground for thousands of years.
People extract more than 200 times as much groundwater from Earth as oil every year.
Groundwater never feeds into lakes, rivers, or wetlands.
qs.note: 本文は逆：It also feeds into lakes, rivers, and wetlands。

qs.q: People extract groundwater only for drinking, never for sanitation or crops.
qs.note: 本文は for drinking, sanitation, watering crops, and other uses と複数の用途を挙げている。

qs.q: Most groundwater is used to water crops.
Groundwater quenches the thirst of some 2 billion people worldwide.
Groundwater quenches the thirst of only a few thousand people worldwide.
qs.note: 本文は some 2 billion people（約20億人）。

qs.q: Less than a quarter of the U.S. population relies on groundwater for drinking water.
qs.note: 本文は half the population of the United States（約半分）。

qs.q: No part of the United States' population relies on groundwater.
qs.note: 本文は half the population of the United States が地下水を利用。

qs.q: Human-caused climate change may increase the demand for groundwater.
Climate change may intensify storms.
Heavier rains are more likely to rush into streams and storm drains than soak into the soil.
Climate change has no effect on how much groundwater is available.
qs.note: 本文は逆：demand for groundwater may rise／there may be less groundwater to go around。

qs.q: Heavier rain always soaks more deeply into the ground, increasing groundwater.
qs.note: 本文は逆：heavier rains rush into streams and storm drains rather than soaking in。

qs.q: Twenty-one of Earth's 37 biggest aquifers are shrinking, according to satellite data.
In California, sucking the ground dry may even be triggering small earthquakes.
All 37 of Earth's biggest aquifers are shrinking.
qs.note: 本文は 37のうち21（Twenty-one of Earth’s 37 biggest aquifers）。

qs.q: The most dried-out aquifers are found deep in untouched rainforests.
qs.note: 本文は near big cities, farms, or arid regions。rainforest ではない。

qs.q: Shrinking aquifers hold more water to refill rivers and streams.
qs.note: 本文は逆：they hold less water to refill rivers and streams。

qs.q: Arsenic from farming or mining seeps into aquifers.
Chemicals injected underground in a process called fracking also pollute groundwater.
Electronic waste from discarded devices and sewage have also tainted groundwater.
Human activity has no effect on the quality of groundwater.
qs.note: 本文は逆：human activity pollutes groundwater in many places。

qs.q: Fracking is a process that purifies groundwater.
qs.note: 本文ではfrackingは地下水を汚染する要因として挙げられている。purifyとは逆。

qs.q: an area of land that is often wet, like a marsh or swamp
a place where water comes up from the ground naturally

qs.q: a very thin wire, generally with a diameter less than or equal to 100 nanometers

qs.q: "while we're working out" = while we're ( ).
qs.note: ハンドアウトP5の書き込みどおり。

qs.q: "To impress ( )." （省略されている1語を補う）
qs.note: 「他人を感心させるため」＝to impress others。ハンドアウトP5どおり。

qs.q: "To comfortably veg out on the couch" = To ( ) on the couch.
qs.note: veg out = vegetateの短縮形で「のんびり過ごす」。ハンドアウトP5どおり。

qs.q: Expressing our unique sense of style is a means of ( ) communication.

qs.note: ハンドアウト見出し "Paragraph 2 – exemplifying (safer) clothes"。

qs.q: How do the "pop-out spikes" actually work, according to Q7?

The spikes are always sticking out, even when standing still.

Paragraph 3 is about shoes, and paragraph 4 is about gloves.
qs.ans: Paragraph 3's clothes keep body heat in, while paragraph 4's clothes let body heat escape.

qs.note: ハンドアウトQ1（Part1, Paragraph1）どおり。

qs.q: Complete the definition of "groundwater": "Groundwater is ___ that ___."
opts: solid ice that floats on the ocean
salt water that fills the seas
qs.note: ハンドアウトQ2のitem/category/characteristics定義どおり。

qs.q: About what percent of Earth's water is seawater?
qs.note: ハンドアウトQ3：淡水が約2.5%なので海水は残り約97.5%。

qs.q: "the meager 1.2 percent" = the small ( ) of 1.2 percent.
"Groundwater is [ hidden / made / lost ] under mountains, plains and even deserts." Which word matches "lurks" in meaning?
qs.note: ハンドアウトP5の丸どおり（lurk≡隠れている）。

qs.q: Complete the definition of "aquifers": "Aquifers are ___ that ___."
opts: buried bodies of water that are held in tiny gaps between rocks and soil grains
qs.ans: buried bodies of water that are held in tiny gaps between rocks and soil grains
qs.note: ハンドアウトQ6の定義どおり。

qs.q: "Aquifers hold about 60 times the ( ) of water in the world’s lakes and rivers combined."
qs.note: ハンドアウトP7どおり（名詞を使った比較表現）。

qs.q: According to Paragraph 4 of the handout, what happens to rain and melted snow?
opts: They seep into the ground and can later surface again as springs, or feed lakes, rivers, and wetlands.
qs.ans: They seep into the ground and can later surface again as springs, or feed lakes, rivers, and wetlands.
qs.note: ハンドアウトP8の書き込み（雨・雪解け水→地下浸透→湧水・湖・川・湿地）どおり。

qs.q: What are people's purposes for using groundwater, according to Q9?
opts: Drinking water, public sanitation, and watering crops
qs.ans: Drinking water, public sanitation, and watering crops
qs.note: ハンドアウトQ9の書き込みどおり。

What effect does "heavier rain" have on groundwater, according to Q13?
opts: Heavy rain rushes straight into rivers and storm drains rather than soaking into the ground, so there may be less groundwater.
Heavy rain always increases the amount of groundwater.
Heavy rain has no effect on groundwater at all.
qs.ans: Heavy rain rushes straight into rivers and storm drains rather than soaking into the ground, so there may be less groundwater.

According to the handout, how should numbers at the beginning of a sentence be written?
qs.note: ハンドアウトP14の注記どおり。

qs.q: What is the implied subject of "threatening" in "...threatening freshwater ecosystems," according to Q15?
opts: the whole preceding situation (groundwater stores holding less water)
qs.ans: the whole preceding situation (groundwater stores holding less water)
qs.note: ハンドアウトQ15どおり（直前の内容全体）。

qs.q: In "sucking the ground dry," what is the grammatical role of "dry," according to Q16?
opts: It is the complement of "the ground" (SVOC), not the object of "sucking."
qs.ans: It is the complement of "the ground" (SVOC), not the object of "sucking."

qs.q: Which word has a meaning similar to "trigger" in this context, according to Q16?
What are the three factors of human activity that pollute groundwater, according to Q17?
opts: Arsenic from farming/mining; chemicals injected underground during fracking; electronic waste and sewage from discarded devices
qs.ans: Arsenic from farming/mining; chemicals injected underground during fracking; electronic waste and sewage from discarded devices
qs.note: ハンドアウトQ17の書き込みどおり。

qs.q: Why may demand for groundwater rise, according to Q2 of the handout?
opts: Because human-caused climate change dries out parts of the planet.
Because more oil is being extracted.
qs.ans: Because human-caused climate change dries out parts of the planet.

qs.q: About what percent of Earth's water is freshwater?
About what percent of Earth’s water is therefore seawater?
Of Earth's freshwater, about what percent is frozen in glaciers and ice caps?
Of Earth's freshwater, about what percent is groundwater?
What percent of freshwater flows through rivers and fills lakes?
How much water do Earth's aquifers hold, compared to the world's lakes and rivers combined?
qs.note: U4 L.13-14。教科書の数字どおり。

qs.q: How much groundwater do people extract from Earth every year, compared to oil?
About how many people worldwide rely on groundwater to quench their thirst?
What portion of the population of the United States relies on groundwater for drinking, according to the passage?
About how many million Americans does "half the population of the United States" represent?

qs.q: The U.S. population (about 340 million) is the third largest in the world, after which two countries?
How many of Earth's 37 biggest aquifers are shrinking, according to satellite data?
Where is groundwater found, according to the passage?
opts: under mountains, plains, and even deserts
qs.ans: under mountains, plains, and even deserts

qs.q: Where are the most dried-out aquifers found?
opts: near big cities, farms, or arid regions
in the North and South Poles

only acid rain and volcanic ash

qs.q: How many words is the Unit 4 reading passage?
qs.note: 教科書 p.29 "(425 words)" 表記どおり。

qs.q: In the Unit 3 experiment, what did stitching conductive thread into a t-shirt turn it into?
opts: an antenna that could send signals to a smartphone
qs.ans: an antenna that could send signals to a smartphone

qs.q: The teacher noted that 30% ÷ 1.2% actually calculates to about how many times, even though the textbook itself says "60 times"?
qs.note: 教科書の本文は "60 times" のまま出題する。教員スライドの指摘（計算上は約25倍）は補足知識として解説にのみ記す。

qs.q: Put the general flow of a debate in the correct order. (Note: only the rebuttal stage starts with the negative side.)
qs.note: Debate #1の図どおり。立論と第二反駁・まとめは「肯定側→否定側」の順だが、第一反駁だけは「否定側→肯定側」の順で始まる（引っかけポイント）。

qs.q: Put the three steps of a Constructive Speech (立論) in the correct order.
items: Give specific evidence for the claim
Restate the team’s position once again
ans: Give specific evidence for the claim
Restate the team’s position once again
qs.note: Debate #1：①チームの立場を明確に述べる ②主張の根拠を具体的に述べる ③自分たちの立場をもう一度述べる。

qs.q: Put the three steps of a Rebuttal Speech (第一反駁) in the correct order.
qs.note: Debate #1：①まず相手チームの主張を要約する ②反論を開始する ③自分たちの立場を再度主張する。

qs.q: What is a debate?
opts: A contest-style discussion in which two teams, the affirmative side and the negative side, argue about a topic
A casual chat between friends about their opinions
A written essay submitted for grading
qs.ans: A contest-style discussion in which two teams, the affirmative side and the negative side, argue about a topic

qs.q: How is a team's side (affirmative or negative) usually decided?
opts: By something like drawing lots, regardless of the speakers' own opinions
Each speaker chooses whichever side they personally agree with
The teacher assigns sides based on the students' grades
qs.ans: By something like drawing lots, regardless of the speakers' own opinions
qs.note: 「自分の意見とは関係なく、クジなどで担当チームが決まる」とある。

qs.q: What determines which team wins a debate?
opts: Convincing the judge with a persuasive argument
qs.ans: Convincing the judge with a persuasive argument
qs.note: 「ジャッジを納得させた方が勝ちとなる」とある。

qs.q: What is the main point (ポイント) of debate, according to the handout?
opts: How angry a speaker can get
How long a speaker can talk
qs.note: 「どれだけ説得力のある議論ができるか」とある。

qs.q: What is the English term for 肯定側?
What is the English term for 否定側?
What is the English term for 審判 (judge)?
What is the English term for 立論?
What is the English term for 第一反駁?
What is the English term for 第二反駁・まとめ?
What is the English term for 判定?
Which side goes first in the Constructive Speech (立論)?
Which side goes first in the Rebuttal Speech (第一反駁)?
opts: Both sides speak at the same time
qs.note: 「反駁だけ否定側からスタートする」引っかけポイント。

qs.q: Which side goes first in the Summary Speech (第二反駁・まとめ)?
About how long is each side's Constructive Speech, including Q&A?
About how long is each side's Rebuttal Speech, including Q&A?
About how long is each side's Summary Speech?
What should be done first in a Constructive Speech?
What is the second step of a Constructive Speech?
opts: Give specific evidence for the claim
Restate the position for the last time
qs.ans: Give specific evidence for the claim

qs.q: What is the final step of a Constructive Speech?
opts: Restate the team's position once again
qs.ans: Restate the team's position once again

qs.q: What should be done first in a Rebuttal Speech?
What comes right after summarizing the opponent's argument in a Rebuttal Speech?
opts: Restate the position for the first time

qs.q: What is the final step of a Rebuttal Speech?
What is the purpose of a Summary Speech?
opts: To summarize each side's arguments while arguing that your own team's position is superior
To introduce the topic for the first time
To ask the other team questions
qs.ans: To summarize each side's arguments while arguing that your own team's position is superior

qs.q: What kind of thinking does debate mainly require?
qs.note: 「ディベートは論理的思考を求められる活動」とある。

qs.q: What is debate NOT about, according to the notes?
opts: Verbally defeating (言い負かす) the opponent
qs.ans: Verbally defeating (言い負かす) the opponent
qs.note: 「相手を言い負かすのではなく」と明記されている。

qs.q: What should be used to persuade the third party (the judge)?
qs.note: 「客観的なデータや理由を使って...説得する論理的なゲーム」とある。

qs.q: What else is emphasized as important during a debate, besides winning?
opts: Respecting teammates' and the opposing team's opinions
Speaking only in the judge's native language
qs.ans: Respecting teammates' and the opposing team's opinions
qs.note: 「チームメイトや相手チームの意見を尊重することも大切」とある。

qs.q: What is emphasized about teamwork in debate?
opts: The whole team should work together on the topic
Only the strongest speaker should talk
Each member should argue a different topic
qs.ans: The whole team should work together on the topic
qs.note: 「チーム一丸となって論題に取り組むことが大切」とある。

qs.q: What is a fact, according to the handout?
opts: Something which can be proven to be true or correct
qs.ans: Something which can be proven to be true or correct
qs.note: How to Express Your Opinions #1どおり。

qs.q: What is an opinion, according to the handout?
opts: What someone thinks or believes, which cannot be proved true or false
A statement backed by scientific evidence
qs.ans: What someone thinks or believes, which cannot be proved true or false
qs.note: How to Express Your Opinions #1どおり。

qs.q: Which words describe a "fact," according to the handout?
qs.note: How to Express Your Opinions #1どおり。

qs.q: Which words describe an "opinion," according to the handout?
qs.note: How to Express Your Opinions #1どおり。

qs.q: Why is "It’s raining now" considered a fact in Example A?
opts: Because you can look outside and check that it is true
Because it is written in a book
qs.ans: Because you can look outside and check that it is true
qs.note: How to Express Your Opinions #1のExample Aどおり。

qs.q: Why is "It’s going to rain later" considered an opinion in Example B?
opts: Because you think it will rain, but you can't be sure
Because rain is always unpredictable by science
qs.ans: Because you think it will rain, but you can't be sure
qs.note: How to Express Your Opinions #1のExample Bどおり。

qs.q: Which modal verbs are recommended to avoid sounding too certain when stating an opinion?
qs.note: 「断定することを避けるためにmay, canなどの助動詞を使うとよい」とある。

qs.q: Which phrase is best for stating a guess with little evidence, according to the handout?
qs.note: 「根拠があまりなく推測する場合」に使う表現として挙げられている。

qs.note: 好みの比較であり証明できない。

qs.note: 公的に定義された事実。

qs.q: Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan.
qs.note: 証明可能な地理的データ。

qs.q: Reading books is more enjoyable than watching movies.
qs.note: 楽しさの比較は個人の感じ方による。

qs.q: The human body is made up of about 60 percent water.
qs.note: 科学的に証明できるデータ。

qs.q: Cats make better pets than dogs.
qs.note: ペットの優劣は個人の好みによる。

qs.note: U4本文で述べられている検証可能な事実。
